# Reviewer (cms-api)

<!-- module-flows:start (generated by .claude/bin/module-index; do not edit) -->

Flows: [`reviewer`](../../flows/reviewer/FLOW.md), [`security-audit`](../../flows/security-audit/FLOW.md).

<!-- module-flows:end -->

## Purpose

Lets a visitor (for example a recruiter) start a 24 h read-only session after a Turnstile check, and lets the owner switch reviewer access on or off and read the session log. Everything answers `404 REVIEWER_FEATURE_OFF` while the deploy switch `REVIEWER_FEATURE_ENABLED` is off ([reviewer flow](../../flows/reviewer/SPEC.md)).

## Techniques

Admission rules are pure (`domain/ReviewerAdmission.rules.ts`: 1 session per IP per 10 min, 200 active at most, `Retry-After`). Session creation runs in one core transaction under an advisory lock, so the cap and the per-IP rule hold under concurrency. The visitor IP is stored only as a keyed HMAC derived from `OTP_PEPPER`. Each session gets an ephemeral `reviewer` account and a 24 h access token with no refresh token; switching the toggle off bumps the reviewer role's `policy_version` and every reviewer account's `token_version`, so live sessions get 401. An in-process interval job deletes accounts whose sessions have all expired. Turnstile fails closed: without a secret, an unconfigured verifier refuses every token.

## Technologies

NestJS; Prisma; Cloudflare Turnstile siteverify over `fetch`; the identity module for access tokens; the shared interval job runner.

## Entry points

`GET /reviewer/status`, `POST /reviewer/sessions` (public, Turnstile), `GET /reviewer/sessions`, `PUT /reviewer/settings` (owner); job `ReviewerCleanupJob`; exports `ReviewerModule`, `REVIEWER_ERROR_CODES`, `REVIEWER_INPUT_LIMITS`.

## Where to change what

Admission limits: `domain/ReviewerAdmission.rules.ts` and `domain/Reviewer.constants.ts` (keep them equal to the canonical values). A new session field: `http/Reviewer.requests.ts`, the repository and the `reviewer_sessions` table. Never store reviewer data in content tables, and keep every route behind the deploy switch check (D2, D2a).
